title: Air Puff for the First Time

patient.name: Ms Nur Hidayah binte Rashid
patient.presenting_complaint: First visit to SNEC for a comprehensive eye check after a colleague was diagnosed with glaucoma

history.hpc: Ms Hidayah is attending SNEC for the first time for a general eye check. She has no visual symptoms but became concerned after a colleague at work was recently diagnosed with glaucoma and was advised to get her own eyes checked, especially since eye pressure tests are part of standard screening. She has never had an eye pressure test before and asks the PSA, 'Will the air puff hurt? My friend said it's quite scary.'
history.pmhx: No known eye conditions. Wears soft contact lenses occasionally for sports. No diabetes, no hypertension.
history.family_hx: No known family history of glaucoma or other eye conditions.
history.social_hx: Preschool teacher. Wears contact lenses 1-2 times a week for sports activities; wearing spectacles today.

iop.right: 16 mmHg — average of three NCT readings (15, 16, 17)
iop.left: 15 mmHg — average of three NCT readings (14, 15, 16)

examination_findings.fundus: Not assessed at this stage — doctor to review

nct.notes: First-time NCT patient. Confirmed no contact lenses worn today. All three readings per eye obtained without blinking or movement on first attempt.

diagnosis: NCT completed for a first-visit patient. Both eyes within normal IOP range (10-21 mmHg). Results recorded for doctor review as part of the comprehensive new-patient work-up.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and explain that this visit will include a general eye check, including a pressure test of the eyes
Ask whether she is wearing contact lenses today — confirm she is wearing spectacles, so no removal of lenses is needed
Perform hand hygiene and wipe all parts of the NCT machine that will contact the patient with alcohol wipes

Explain the procedure clearly since this is her first time: 'I will measure the pressure inside your eye using a gentle puff of air. It may feel like a quick tap of air on your eye — it does not hurt and there is no needle or contact with your eye.'
Position her comfortably at the machine: forehead against the rest, chin on the chinrest, eyes open and looking at the fixation light
Reassure her calmly before the first puff: 'You'll hear a small click and feel a puff of air — try to keep your eyes open and look at the green light.'
Perform NCT on the right eye first, taking three readings
Repeat for the left eye, taking three readings
If she blinks or moves during a reading, discard it and repeat — reassure her this is normal and not a problem
Wipe the machine's contact parts with alcohol wipes and perform hand hygiene after the test
Record all six readings (three per eye) and the averages clearly in SCM
follow_up: Hand the completed IOP results to the doctor along with VA results as part of her new-patient work-up
Note in the form that this was her first NCT and she tolerated it well
patient_education: Reassure Ms Hidayah that the test is now complete and she did well
Explain that the doctor will review all her results together as part of her comprehensive eye check
Do not tell her whether her eye pressure is 'normal' or 'high' — this is for the doctor to discuss
If she asks about her colleague's glaucoma diagnosis and her own risk, advise her to raise this directly with the doctor

key_points: Confirms patient identity and reason for visit (first visit, general check)
Checks whether the patient is wearing contact lenses before NCT
Acknowledges the patient's nervousness about the air puff with reassurance, without over-promising 'it won't hurt at all'
Notes the family/social context (colleague's glaucoma diagnosis) as background only, without speculating on the patient's own risk
Performs hand hygiene and wipes machine contact parts before and after the test
Positions the patient correctly: forehead rest, chin rest, eyes open, fixating on the target
Takes three readings per eye, right eye first, and calculates the average
Discards and repeats any reading affected by blinking or movement
Records all individual readings and averages clearly in SCM
Does not tell the patient whether her IOP readings are normal or abnormal
Recognises both readings fall within the normal 10-21 mmHg range but still defers interpretation to the doctor
Notes that this is part of a new-patient work-up and other tests (VA, etc.) should accompany the IOP results
Does not speculate about the patient's personal glaucoma risk based on her colleague's diagnosis
Explains the NCT procedure clearly and reassuringly for a first-time patient
Handles the patient's anxiety about the air puff with empathy and accurate, non-alarming information
Documents all results accurately and hands them to the doctor
Redirects clinical questions about glaucoma risk to the doctor
